key_insight: APS-produced Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings remained predominantly crystalline, while increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance at the expense of corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: A 90 mm spray distance offered the most favourable tested balance of mechanical performance and electrochemical behaviour.
method: Deposited low-glass-forming-ability Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at varied spray distances.
Examined phase composition, lamellar microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluated hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
evidence_signal: XRD detected α-Fe(Si) and Fe–Zr intermetallic phases with no detectable amorphous fraction, while coating porosity ranged from 2.2% to 4.9%.
watch_item: The 90 mm result is specific to the investigated conditions; longer spray distances increased porosity and interlamellar defects, compromising corrosion resistance.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
